To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain has a limited capacity to buffer the extracellular acidosis that develops in cerebral ischemia.
iron chelation is neuroprotective in a rat model of focal cerebral ischemia and that iron is released from intracellular stores in the ischemic brain.
iron is a key factor in the development of acidosis and cerebral edema in ischemic stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of iron in the brain in ischemia.
the development of new, more effective and less toxic iron chelators for treatment of iron overload disorders and cancer.
the development and characterization of new iron chelators, and their application to the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to support the hypothesis that iron is a causative factor in cerebral ischemic injury.
the use of iron chelation therapy in patients with neurologic disorders is not recommended.
the use of iron in patients with cerebral ischemia is not supported by current evidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most significant factor in our study was the presence of a low molecular weight iron in the cerebral ischemic acidotic brain, which was not found in the non-ischemic control brain.
the results indicate that iron is a significant contributor to the pathophysiology of brain injury after cerebral ischemia.
it is not possible to predict the effects of an intervention in the brain of a patient with a specific disease based on the results of an animal study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a combination of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and aspirin to achieve a high level of anticoagulation in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
the use of the iron chelator deferoxamine (DFO) in a rat model of focal cerebral ischemic acidotic stroke significantly reduced the size of the ischemic lesion and improved the neurological score.

the iron in the blood can be a major contributor to brain injury in the setting of stroke and other forms of brain injury, but that it is also a very important part of the brain’s ability to repair itself after a stroke or other brain injury.
